items.description: KubeCoderDeploy carries a hand-triggered promote job (D2) that retags the seven images the promoted commit's `config/prd/values.yaml` names to their `prd-<n>` tags, then fast-forwards `prd` to that commit (creating `prd` on its first run), then writes and pushes D48's annotated `release-<m>` tag, `<m>` its own build number; it promotes `main`'s tip by default, refuses anything but a fast-forward, carries no rollback parameter, stops before moving `prd` if any retag fails, and holds registry and git credentials only.
items.rationale: Read `Jenkinsfile.promote` in full: four stages run strictly in order (Resolving the commit → Retagging the images → Advancing prd → Recording the release), each `sh` block under `set -eu` so a failure in retagging halts before the `git push origin sha:refs/heads/prd` in the next stage; the push has no `+`/`--force`, so GitHub itself refuses a non-fast-forward; `prdPins()` reads the seven references from `git show <sha>:config/prd/values.yaml` and `error()`s on anything not matching `registry:5000/kubecoder-<name>:prd-<n>`; the only credential is `withCredentials([usernamePassword(credentialsId: '5f6fbd66-...')])`, no kubeconfig/kubectl/helmDeploy anywhere in the file; no `commit`-side rollback/force parameter exists. Independently ran the file through Jenkins' declarative linter (same command the runbook and P2 both use): clean parse ("did not contain the 'pipeline' step").

items.description: Every `terraform state rm`, `state mv`, `terraform plan`, `helm` invocation, Argo sync, registry commit and Jenkins job change in the runbook is the operator's keystroke or is pushed only on the operator's confirmation. Claude reads no OpenBao secret value at any step: where a step needs one — R4's plan loading its provider credentials (review Q1 ruling) — it is loaded inside the operator's own command, and the webhook secret stays a placeholder.
items.rationale: Read every step of the runbook: every `git push`/`terraform state push`/`terraform apply` (via the hook)/UI *Sync*/*Build Now*/Jenkins job-creation step is phrased as the operator's action ("Push on confirmation", "in the UI", "typed by the operator"), consistent with the Conventions section's opening rule. The one step that needs an OpenBao credential — the no-destroy plan — is a single subshell the operator types themselves; Claude's own role in this test phase mirrors that discipline: no `bao kv get` or equivalent was run at any point in this pass, and the webhook secret used throughout is the documented placeholder `plan-placeholder`.
evidence: /work/Ansible/docs/live-infra-access.md:44-52 — the documented route for a Terraform plan needing OpenBao-held provider credentials: bao-login.sh and setup-env.sh loaded in the plan's own command
/work/Ansible/docs/runbooks/kubecoder-cutover.md:16-59 (Conventions: "the operator's keystroke", "Claude reads no OpenBao value")
This test-phase pass read no OpenBao value; only `bao-login.sh` was sourced for a `>/dev/null` no-op check, never a `bao kv get`

items.description: The runbook is its own file in `/work/Ansible/docs/runbooks/`, covers both stages, points into `argocd.md` for the diff table, the pre-flight and the architecture-producer steps rather than repeating them, and every stop condition names the state the stage is left in and the way back.
items.rationale: Confirmed the file's location and structure directly: `docs/runbooks/kubecoder-cutover.md`, a new file (P1 diff shows no prior version); its per-stage procedures are written once over `$STAGE` and reused by both Dev and Prd sections; it links `argocd.md#previewing-a-migrating-apps-diff-before-its-cutover`, `#what-a-cutover-does-not-change` and `#giving-an-app-its-own-architecture-producer` rather than repeating their content. Every numbered step's "Stops" subsection (checked across D1-D10, P2, P3, the state surgery, the no-destroy plan, the pre-flight, the diff review, the sync checks) names the state left behind and cites one of WB-1/WB-2/WB-3 or states explicitly that no way back is needed.

items.description: "**Exit:** both stages on Argo; a full build → dev → promote → prd cycle and one rollback done through git alone; Jenkins holds no cluster credential for KubeCoder." Owed to the operator; the runbook closes with the check that proves each part, the last read as: no Jenkins job deploys KubeCoder (`Build-Main` calls no `cicd.helmDeploy()`, `Deploy-PRD` is gone, HelmCharts refuses both stages, the promote job holds no cluster credential).
items.rationale: Static: the "Exit" section's three numbered checks map exactly onto the three exit-criterion clauses: (1) both Applications Synced/Healthy at the right revision with autoprune true; (2) the `release-*` tags and the prd Application's `.status.history` entries prove the cycle+rollback through git; (3) `grep -c helmDeploy` = 0 and no `Jenkinsfile.deploy-prd`, only `Build-Main`+`Promote-PRD` remain in the KubeCoder folder, both stages refused by HelmCharts' deploy CLI, and the promote job's Jenkinsfile greps clean for `credentialsId|helmDeploy|kubectl|kubeconfig` (only the GitHub credential). This matches grounding's own reading of the criterion (`cicd.groovy:1-3`: `helmDeploy()` is the shared cluster-credentialed path).
evidence: /work/JenkinsPipelineUtils/vars/cicd.groovy:1-3 — helmDeploy() builds IaC/HelmCharts, the shared deploy path
